title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the page and the crossed-out lines. S is a graded algebra over k_0, generated in degree 1: the crossed-out line contains Hom_{k_0}(S_1, P_{i+1}). M is the category of graded S-modules. M_N is the full subcategory of modules with M_i = 0 for i < N. For N ≤ N', the functor τ_{N',N}: M_N → M_{N'} is truncation, M ↦ M_{≥N'}.

First paragraph. Grothendieck notes that τ_{N',N} is exact and commutes with filtered colimits (lim→). He also notes it is a localization functor: it is the projection of M_N onto its quotient by the localizing (thick, lim→-stable) Serre subcategory ker τ = {M : M_i = 0 for i ≥ N'}. M_{N'} is then identified with that quotient.

Second part: the right adjoint ρ_{N,N'} of τ_{N',N}.
- The adjunction sought is Hom_{M_{N'}}(τM, P) ≅ Hom_{M_N}(M, ρP).
- He observes that Hom_{M_{N'}}(τM, P) = Hom_M(τM, P), and that this sits inside ∏_{i≥N'} Hom_k(M_i, P_i). The diagram of M against P (zero below N') pictures this.
- After a crossed-out attempt via products of Hom_{k_0}(S_1, P_{i+j}), he obtains the formula by Yoneda. The free module S(-i), i.e. T^{-i}S, lies in M_N exactly when i ≥ N. So ρ(P)_i = Hom_{M_N}(S(-i), ρP) = Hom(τ_{≥N'}(S(-i)), P) = Hom^i_M(τ_{≥N'-i}S, P) for i ≥ N, and ρ(P)_i = 0 for i < N.
- For i ≥ N' this gives back P_i, so τρ ≅ id. Hence ρ is fully faithful, which confirms that τ is a Gabriel localization.

Interpretation. This is the graded-module form of Serre's comparison between graded modules and quasi-coherent sheaves on Proj. Taking the colimit over N' of Hom(S_{≥N'-i}, P) gives the section module Γ_*. In this notebook it is presumably preliminary bookkeeping for comparing truncated categories of graded modules. The surrounding pages concern divided-power de Rham complexes: the previous page treats PD-structures on graded alternating DG algebras.
errors: The final isomorphism is written Hom_{M_N}(T^{-i}τ_{N'-i}S, P). Since P ∈ M_{N'} and T^{-i}τ_{N'-i}S is concentrated in degrees ≥ N', the subscript is harmless (both Homs agree), but the logically natural one is M_{N'} or simply M.
The claim that the quotient of M_N by ker τ is equivalent to M_{N'} is stated without proof. It follows from the computation τρ ≅ id (ρ fully faithful), which the page implicitly gives. No real gap.

ideas.what: Truncation τ_{≥N'} on graded modules as an exact, colimit-preserving quotient by the localizing Serre subcategory of modules vanishing in degrees ≥ N'
ideas.modern_name: Gabriel localization / Serre quotient of abelian categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel (1962, Des catégories abéliennes); Serre (FAC 1955) for the graded/Proj case
ideas.where_published: Tôhoku (1957) treats quotient categories; EGA II §2 treats graded modules and Proj

ideas.what: Explicit right adjoint ρ(P)_i = Hom^i(τ_{≥N'-i}S, P) for i ≥ N, computed by Yoneda on free modules S(-i)
ideas.modern_name: Section functor of the localization; truncated version of Γ_* (graded Hom from the irrelevant-ideal powers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (FAC), Gabriel; standard in noncommutative projective geometry (Artin–Zhang 1994)
ideas.where_published: EGA II §2.7–2.9 / EGA III §2 (Γ_* and the comparison between graded modules and sheaves on Proj)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Serre/Gabriel localization for graded modules, with a routine Yoneda computation of the right adjoint. This is working bookkeeping inside the divided-power de Rham notes, not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: First line: τ_{N',N} is written with indices N', N (the transcription is correct). The phrase is 'un foncteur de localisation exact, commutant aux lim→' (direct limits).
'ss-catégorie localisante épaisse stable par lim→' — the lim is underlined with a rightward arrow, i.e. lim→.
In the definition line 'M_i (τ_{N',N}M = 0 i.e.) M_i = 0 pour i ≥ N'', the first 'M_i' overwrites an 'M_0'.
In the crossed-out block the term reads Hom_{k_0}(S_1, P_{i+1}), with an index i+1 rather than i+j.
The final line reads 'si i ≥ N', which is the condition for the second case of the formula for ρ_{N,N'}(P)_i.
